patch_description: The current program only uses a repulsion relaxation, which plateaus at ratio^2 ≈ 0.22 (score 0.93). Prior generations showed that adding (a) an annealed soft-min/soft-max L-BFGS polish and (b) a vectorized steepest-ascent hill climb that moves all binding min/max pairs simultaneously (the "multi-pair binding-constraint" strategy from the recommendations) pushes the score to ~0.94+. I add both as post-processing stages: every relax result gets a short polish + climb, and the final winner gets a high-precision polish and a multi-pair climb. This is targeted: the relax stage stays as the global basin search, while the new stages do the fine convergence on the true objective. To stay within timeout, climb uses multi-pair candidate generation (all pairs within 5% of dmin/dmax) and polish uses a small tau ladder.
